people.name: Solomon
people.role: King who builds the temple and later turns away
people.relations: Son of David and Bathsheba. Father of Rehoboam.
people.meaning: David has him anointed king at Gihon. He asks God for an understanding heart and builds the temple. Later his wives turn his heart to other gods. The LORD says he will tear the kingdom from Solomon’s son.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Adonijah
people.role: Royal son who claims the throne
people.relations: Son of David and Haggith. Half-brother of Solomon.
people.meaning: He says, “I will be king,” and holds a feast with Joab and Abiathar. The feast ends when Solomon is anointed. Later he asks for Abishag as his wife. Solomon has Benaiah kill him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abishag
people.role: Young Shunammite who serves the aging David
people.relations: She serves King David. Adonijah later asks to marry her.
people.meaning: She is brought to keep the old king warm, and she serves him. After David dies, Adonijah asks Bathsheba to get her as his wife. Solomon hears the request as a claim on the kingdom and has Adonijah killed.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The two women before Solomon
people.role: Two unnamed women who both claim one baby
people.relations: Both live in one house, and each has a baby. The text calls them prostitutes.
people.meaning: One woman’s baby dies in the night. Each tells Solomon the living child is hers. Solomon calls for a sword to cut the child in two. One woman begs him to let the child live, and Solomon names her the mother.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pharaoh’s daughter, Solomon’s wife
people.role: Unnamed Egyptian wife of Solomon
people.relations: Daughter of Pharaoh and wife of Solomon. She is not the princess who finds Moses.
people.meaning: Solomon marries her to join with Pharaoh king of Egypt. She lives in David’s city until Solomon builds her a house. Pharaoh gives her the city of Gezer as a wedding gift.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Adoniram
people.role: Official over Solomon’s forced labor
people.relations: Son of Abda. Serves Solomon.
people.meaning: He is over the men Solomon forces to work. Solomon sends thirty thousand of them to Lebanon in turns. He may be the Adoram of chapter 12, but that is a proposal.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hiram, the bronze worker
people.role: Bronze worker who makes the temple pieces
people.relations: His mother is a widow of Naphtali. His father is a bronze worker of Tyre. He is not King Hiram.
people.meaning: Solomon brings him from Tyre. He casts the two bronze pillars, the sea, and the ten bases. He also makes the pots, shovels, and basins for the LORD’s house.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The queen of Sheba
people.role: Unnamed queen who tests Solomon with questions
people.relations: She visits Solomon from her own land with her servants.
people.meaning: She hears of Solomon’s fame and comes to test him with hard questions. He answers them all. She praises his wisdom and blesses the LORD. She gives him gold, spices, and precious stones, then goes home.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hadad
people.role: Edomite royal child who flees to Egypt
people.relations: One of the king’s offspring in Edom. Husband of Tahpenes’s sister and father of Genubath.
people.meaning: Joab kills the males of Edom, and the child Hadad flees to Egypt. Pharaoh gives him a house, land, and a wife. When David and Joab die, he asks Pharaoh to let him go home. The LORD raises him as an enemy of Solomon.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Rezon
people.role: Enemy of Solomon who rules in Damascus
people.relations: Son of Eliada. He flees from his lord, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
people.meaning: He gathers men and leads a troop. They settle in Damascus, and he rules Syria. He is an enemy to Israel all the days of Solomon.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jeroboam
people.role: First king of the northern tribes
people.relations: Son of Nebat and the widow Zeruah. Father of Abijah and Nadab.
people.meaning: Solomon puts him over the labor of the house of Joseph. Ahijah tears a garment and promises him ten tribes. He flees to Egypt, returns, and becomes king of Israel. He then makes two gold calves so the people will not go to Jerusalem.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahijah, the Shilonite
people.role: Prophet who promises Jeroboam ten tribes
people.relations: From Shiloh. He is not the scribe Ahijah or Baasha’s father Ahijah.
people.meaning: He tears a new garment into twelve pieces and gives Jeroboam ten. The ten pieces stand for ten tribes. Later he is old and cannot see. He still knows Jeroboam’s disguised wife and says her child will die.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Rehoboam
people.role: King whose harsh answer divides Israel
people.relations: Son of Solomon and Naamah. Father of Abijam.
people.meaning: The people ask him at Shechem to make their work lighter. He drops the old men’s advice and promises a heavier yoke. Israel turns from him, and he keeps Judah. In his fifth year Shishak takes the temple treasures.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shishak
people.role: King of Egypt who attacks Jerusalem
people.relations: Jeroboam flees to him. He later attacks Rehoboam’s city.
people.meaning: Jeroboam stays in Egypt with him until Solomon dies. In Rehoboam’s fifth year he comes against Jerusalem. He takes the treasures of the LORD’s house and the king’s house. He also takes Solomon’s gold shields.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Tahpenes
people.role: Queen of Egypt in Hadad’s story
people.relations: Wife of Pharaoh. Her sister marries Hadad.
people.meaning: Pharaoh gives her sister to Hadad as wife. Tahpenes weans their son Genubath in Pharaoh’s house. The text says nothing more about her.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Genubath
people.role: Son of Hadad raised in Egypt
people.relations: Son of Hadad. His mother is the sister of Tahpenes.
people.meaning: Tahpenes weans him in Pharaoh’s house. He lives there among Pharaoh’s sons. The text names him in one verse and tells no more.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shemaiah
people.role: Man of God who stops Rehoboam’s war
people.relations: He speaks to Rehoboam, Judah, and Benjamin.
people.meaning: Rehoboam gathers 180,000 warriors to win Israel back. Shemaiah gives God’s word: do not fight your brothers. The men listen and go home.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Adoram
people.role: Forced-labor official stoned by Israel
people.relations: He serves Rehoboam. He may be the Adoniram of chapters 4 and 5, but that is a proposal.
people.meaning: He is over the men forced to work. Rehoboam sends him after Israel turns away. All Israel stones him to death, and Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem in his chariot.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The man of God from Judah
people.role: Unnamed man of God who speaks against Bethel’s altar
people.relations: He comes from Judah. He faces Jeroboam and then meets the old prophet of Bethel.
people.meaning: He cries out against Jeroboam’s altar, and the altar splits. Jeroboam’s hand dries up, and the man prays until it is healed. He was told not to eat or drink there. An old prophet lies to him, and he eats. A lion kills him on the road.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The older prophet at Bethel
people.role: Unnamed old prophet who lies to the man of God
people.relations: He lives in Bethel. His sons tell him what the man of God did.
people.meaning: He rides after the man of God. He lies that an angel said to bring him home. At the table he speaks the LORD’s word against his guest. Later he buries the man in his own grave.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jeroboam’s wife
people.role: Unnamed mother who visits Ahijah in disguise
people.relations: Wife of Jeroboam. Mother of the sick child Abijah.
people.meaning: Jeroboam sends her to Shiloh in disguise with bread, cakes, and honey. Ahijah cannot see, yet he knows her at the door. He gives her heavy news for Jeroboam’s house. She reaches Tirzah, and the child dies as she steps in.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abijah, Jeroboam’s son
people.role: Sick son of King Jeroboam
people.relations: Son of Jeroboam and his unnamed wife.
people.meaning: He falls sick, and his mother goes to ask Ahijah about him. He dies when she comes home. All Israel buries him and mourns. He is not Abijam, the king of Judah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Naamah
people.role: Ammonite mother of Rehoboam
people.relations: Mother of Rehoboam. The text calls her the Ammonitess.
people.meaning: The text names her twice as Rehoboam’s mother. It tells nothing that she does.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abijam
people.role: King of Judah between Rehoboam and Asa
people.relations: Son of Rehoboam. Maacah is called his mother.
people.meaning: He rules three years in Jerusalem. He walks in his father’s sins and is at war with Jeroboam. The LORD still gives him a son to rule after him, for David’s sake.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Asa
people.role: King of Judah who removes idols and pays Syria
people.relations: Son of Abijam. Father of Jehoshaphat.
people.meaning: He removes the idols and removes Maacah from being queen. The high places stay. When Baasha builds Ramah, Asa sends the temple’s silver and gold to Ben Hadad. Ben Hadad attacks Israel, and Asa builds Geba and Mizpah with Ramah’s stones.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Maacah
people.role: Queen mother removed by Asa
people.relations: Daughter of Abishalom. The text calls her mother of Abijam and of Asa.
people.meaning: She makes an image for an Asherah. Asa removes her from being queen. He cuts down her image and burns it at the brook Kidron.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ben Hadad, Asa’s ally
people.role: King of Syria paid to attack Israel
people.relations: Son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion. The Ben Hadad who fights Ahab in chapter 20 appears to be a later king.
people.meaning: Asa sends him silver and gold and asks him to break his treaty with Baasha. He agrees. His captains strike Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, and the land of Naphtali. Baasha then stops building Ramah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nadab
people.role: King of Israel killed by Baasha
people.relations: Son of Jeroboam.
people.meaning: He rules Israel two years and walks in his father’s way. Baasha kills him while Israel attacks Gibbethon. Baasha then kills all the house of Jeroboam.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Baasha
people.role: King of Israel who kills Nadab
people.relations: Son of Ahijah of Issachar, who is not the prophet Ahijah. Father of Elah.
people.meaning: He kills Nadab at Gibbethon and wipes out Jeroboam’s house. He rules from Tirzah for twenty-four years and fights Asa. He builds Ramah but stops when Ben Hadad attacks. Jehu the son of Hanani tells him his own house will fall.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehu, Hanani’s son
people.role: Prophet who speaks against Baasha’s house
people.relations: Son of Hanani. He is not Jehu the son of Nimshi.
people.meaning: He brings the LORD’s word against Baasha. Baasha walked in Jeroboam’s way, so his house will be swept away. Zimri later kills all the house of Baasha, as Jehu said.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Elah
people.role: King of Israel killed by his officer
people.relations: Son of Baasha. Zimri kills him at Tirzah.
people.meaning: He rules Israel two years in Tirzah. He is drinking in Arza’s house when Zimri strikes him dead. Zimri then kills all the house of Baasha.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zimri
people.role: Chariot officer who rules for seven days
people.relations: Servant of Elah and captain of half his chariots. Omri’s army comes against him.
people.meaning: He kills Elah and all the house of Baasha. The army hears and makes Omri king. Omri takes Tirzah. Zimri burns the king’s house over himself and dies after seven days.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Omri
people.role: Army commander who becomes king and builds Samaria
people.relations: Opponent of Tibni. Father of Ahab.
people.meaning: The army makes him king in the camp at Gibbethon. He takes Tirzah from Zimri and then beats Tibni’s side. He buys a hill from Shemer and builds Samaria. The text says he did more evil than all before him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Tibni
people.role: Rival of Omri for the throne
people.relations: Son of Ginath.
people.meaning: Half the people follow Tibni to make him king. Half follow Omri. Omri’s side wins, Tibni dies, and Omri rules. The text does not say how Tibni dies.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shemer
people.role: Owner of the hill of Samaria
people.relations: He sells his hill to Omri.
people.meaning: Omri buys the hill from him for two talents of silver. Omri builds a city there and names it Samaria after Shemer.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahab
people.role: King of Israel faced by Elijah and Micaiah
people.relations: Son of Omri. Husband of Jezebel. Father of Ahaziah.
people.meaning: He marries Jezebel and builds an altar for Baal in Samaria. He beats Ben Hadad twice but lets him go. He takes Naboth’s vineyard after Jezebel has Naboth killed. He ignores Micaiah’s warning and dies of an arrow wound at Ramoth Gilead.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jezebel
people.role: Queen who threatens Elijah and has Naboth killed
people.relations: Daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. Wife of Ahab.
people.meaning: She cuts off the LORD’s prophets. After Carmel she swears to kill Elijah. She writes letters in Ahab’s name so Naboth is accused and stoned. The LORD says dogs will eat her by Jezreel’s wall.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hiel
people.role: Man of Bethel who builds Jericho
people.relations: Father of Abiram and Segub.
people.meaning: He builds Jericho in Ahab’s days. He lays its base at the loss of Abiram, his firstborn. He sets up its gates at the loss of Segub, his youngest. The text says this matches the LORD’s word by Joshua.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Elijah
people.role: Prophet who stands against Ahab and Baal
people.relations: A Tishbite from the settlers of Gilead. He calls Elisha to follow him.
people.meaning: He tells Ahab no rain will fall, then hides at Cherith and Zarephath. On Mount Carmel he prays, fire falls, and he kills the prophets of Baal. He runs from Jezebel to Horeb, where the LORD gives him new work. He later tells Ahab his house will fall for Naboth’s death.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The widow of Zarephath
people.role: Unnamed widow who feeds Elijah
people.relations: Mother of a son who falls sick and lives again.
people.meaning: She has one handful of meal and a little oil. She bakes for Elijah first, and the jars do not run out. When her son stops breathing, she blames Elijah. Elijah gives him back alive, and she calls Elijah a man of God.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The widow’s son
people.role: Unnamed boy whom Elijah’s prayer brings back
people.relations: Son of the widow at Zarephath.
people.meaning: He falls sick until no breath is left in him. Elijah stretches over him three times and cries to the LORD. The child’s soul comes back, and Elijah gives him to his mother.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Obadiah
people.role: Palace official who hides the LORD’s prophets
people.relations: He is over Ahab’s household and fears the LORD greatly.
people.meaning: He hides one hundred prophets from Jezebel in caves and feeds them. Ahab sends him to look for grass, and he meets Elijah. He fears Ahab will kill him if Elijah is gone. He still goes and tells Ahab.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Elijah’s unnamed servant
people.role: Helper who watches for the cloud
people.relations: He serves Elijah. The text does not name him.
people.meaning: On Carmel, Elijah sends him seven times to look toward the sea. The seventh time he sees a small cloud like a man’s hand. Elijah sends him to warn Ahab of rain. Elijah later leaves his servant at Beersheba.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Elisha
people.role: Farmer whom Elijah calls with his mantle
people.relations: Son of Shaphat. From Abel Meholah.
people.meaning: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint him prophet in Elijah’s place. Elijah finds him plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and puts his mantle on him. Elisha kills his oxen, feeds the people, and follows Elijah. His later work is in 2 Kings.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hazael
people.role: Man the LORD names as Syria’s next king
people.relations: The LORD names him to Elijah at Horeb, with Jehu and Elisha.
people.meaning: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint Hazael king over Syria. The LORD speaks of the sword of Hazael. Hazael does nothing in this book. His rise is told in 2 Kings.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehu, Nimshi’s son
people.role: Man the LORD names as Israel’s future king
people.relations: Son of Nimshi. He is not the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani.
people.meaning: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint Jehu king over Israel. Jehu will kill those who escape Hazael’s sword. He does nothing in this book. 2 Kings tells how he takes power.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ben Hadad, Ahab’s opponent
people.role: King of Syria beaten and freed by Ahab
people.relations: Thirty-two kings march with him. He appears to be a later king than Asa’s ally Ben Hadad.
people.meaning: He attacks Samaria and demands Ahab’s silver, gold, wives, and children. Israel beats him while he is drinking. The next year he loses again at Aphek and hides in an inner room. Ahab calls him brother, makes a covenant, and lets him go.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The prophets who counsel Ahab
people.role: Unnamed prophets who speak to Ahab in chapter 20
people.relations: They speak to Ahab during the wars with Ben Hadad. They are not the four hundred prophets of chapter 22.
people.meaning: A prophet tells Ahab the LORD will give him the great army. A man of God promises a second win at Aphek. After Ahab frees Ben Hadad, one of the prophets waits for him in disguise. He tells Ahab his life will pay for the man he let go.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Naboth
people.role: Jezreelite killed through false accusations
people.relations: A man of Jezreel. His vineyard lies next to Ahab’s palace.
people.meaning: Ahab offers to buy or trade for his vineyard. Naboth says he will not give up the land of his fathers. Jezebel has two men accuse him of cursing God and the king. He is stoned to death, and Ahab goes to take the vineyard.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.role: King of Judah who asks for the LORD’s word
people.relations: Son of Asa and Azubah. Father of Jehoram.
people.meaning: He agrees to go with Ahab to Ramoth Gilead. He asks for the LORD’s word first, and then for one more prophet. In battle the Syrians take him for Ahab until he cries out. He rules Judah twenty-five years and makes peace with Israel.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Micaiah
people.role: Prophet who warns Ahab before battle
people.relations: Son of Imlah. Ahab hates him and puts him in prison.
people.meaning: Told to agree with the other prophets, he first says, “Go up and prosper.” Ahab demands the truth. He tells of Israel scattered like sheep and of a lying spirit the LORD sent. Zedekiah strikes him, and Ahab sends him to prison.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.role: Prophet who opposes Micaiah
people.relations: Son of Chenaanah. He is not the later king of Judah named Zedekiah.
people.meaning: He makes iron horns and says Ahab will push the Syrians with them. When Micaiah speaks of a lying spirit, he strikes Micaiah on the cheek. Micaiah says he will hide in an inner room.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Amon
people.role: City governor ordered to hold Micaiah
people.relations: He is named with Joash the king’s son. He is not the later king of Judah named Amon.
people.meaning: Ahab orders Micaiah taken back to him. He is to keep Micaiah in prison on bread and water until Ahab returns. The text names him in one verse.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joash
people.role: King’s son told to hold Micaiah
people.relations: Called the king’s son. He is named with Amon the governor.
people.meaning: Ahab sends Micaiah back to him and to Amon. They are to keep Micaiah in prison until Ahab returns in peace. The text names him in one verse.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ahaziah
people.role: King of Israel after Ahab
people.relations: Son of Ahab.
people.meaning: He becomes king in Samaria and rules two years. He asks to send his servants in Jehoshaphat’s ships, and Jehoshaphat refuses. He serves Baal as his father did. His story goes on in 2 Kings.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joab
people.role: Army captain who backs Adonijah
people.relations: Son of Zeruiah. Brother of Abishai and Asahel.
people.meaning: He helps Adonijah and eats at his feast. David tells Solomon that Joab killed Abner and Amasa in peace time. When Adonijah dies, Joab flees to the altar. Benaiah kills him there on Solomon’s order.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nathan
people.role: Prophet who helps Solomon become king
people.relations: He speaks to Bathsheba and to David. He works with Zadok and Benaiah.
people.meaning: He tells Bathsheba that Adonijah is acting as king. He sends her to David and then comes in to back her words. David orders Solomon made king. Nathan and Zadok anoint Solomon at Gihon.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hiram
people.role: King of Tyre who sends Solomon wood and gold
people.relations: He always loved David and makes a treaty with Solomon. He is not Hiram the bronze worker.
people.meaning: He sends Solomon cedar and cypress wood, and Solomon pays in wheat and oil. Solomon gives him twenty cities in Galilee, and they do not please him. His sailors go with Solomon’s ships to Ophir for gold.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zadok
people.role: Priest who anoints Solomon
people.relations: Son of Ahitub. Father of Ahimaaz.
people.meaning: He does not join Adonijah. At David’s order he takes the horn of oil from the Tent and anoints Solomon. Solomon then puts him in Abiathar’s place as priest.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Benaiah
people.role: Officer who carries out Solomon’s death orders
people.relations: Son of Jehoiada. From Kabzeel.
people.meaning: He does not join Adonijah and helps bring Solomon to Gihon. On Solomon’s orders he kills Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei. Solomon puts him over the army in Joab’s place.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Bathsheba
people.role: Solomon’s mother who speaks for him to David
people.relations: Daughter of Eliam. Wife of Uriah, later wife of David. Mother of Solomon.
people.meaning: Nathan warns her, and she reminds David of his oath that Solomon will rule. David swears it again that day. Later Adonijah asks her to seek Abishag for him. She carries the request to Solomon, and Solomon has Adonijah killed.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shimei
people.role: Benjamite told not to leave Jerusalem
people.relations: Son of Gera. From Bahurim.
people.meaning: David tells Solomon that Shimei once cursed him. Solomon orders Shimei to stay in Jerusalem or die. After three years Shimei goes to Gath to bring back two slaves. Solomon has Benaiah kill him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jonathan, Abiathar’s son
people.role: Messenger who reports Solomon’s anointing
people.relations: Son of Abiathar the priest. He brings news to Adonijah.
people.meaning: He comes to Adonijah’s feast as the trumpet sounds. Adonijah expects good news. Jonathan says David has made Solomon king and Solomon sits on the throne. The guests are afraid and leave.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Amasa
people.role: Army captain whom Joab killed
people.relations: Son of Jether. His mother Abigail is the sister of Zeruiah.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. David tells Solomon that Joab killed him and Abner. Solomon gives this as a reason for Joab’s death.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Barzillai
people.role: Gileadite who once helped David
people.relations: A Gileadite. His sons came to David when David fled from Absalom.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. David tells Solomon to show kindness to his sons. They are to eat at Solomon’s table.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abner
people.role: Army captain whom Joab killed
people.relations: Son of Ner. Captain of the army of Israel.
people.meaning: He does not act in this book. David tells Solomon that Joab killed him and Amasa. Solomon calls both men better than Joab.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abiathar
people.role: Priest removed after supporting Adonijah
people.relations: Son of Ahimelech and father of Jonathan. He carried the ark before David.
people.meaning: He helps Adonijah and eats at his feast. Solomon says he deserves death but spares him for his service to David. Solomon ends his work as priest and sends him to Anathoth. Chapter 4 still lists him as a priest.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: David
people.role: Aging king who names Solomon as successor
people.relations: Son of Jesse. Father of Amnon, Absalom, Tamar, Solomon, and other children.
people.meaning: He is old and cold when Adonijah claims the throne. Bathsheba and Nathan remind him of his oath, and he has Solomon anointed. He tells Solomon to keep God’s law and to deal with Joab and Shimei. After his death the LORD spares part of the kingdom for his sake.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

places.name: Gath · Tell es-Safi
places.summary: Two of Shimei’s slaves run away to Achish, king of Gath, in chapter 2. Shimei goes there and brings them back. Solomon has him killed for leaving Jerusalem.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Elijah runs from Jezebel to Beersheba in chapter 19. He leaves his servant there and walks on into the wilderness.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: David has Solomon made king here in chapter 1. Solomon builds the temple and his own house here. Shishak takes the city’s treasures in chapter 14.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Gibeon
places.summary: Solomon offers sacrifices at Gibeon in chapter 3. The LORD appears to him there in a dream. Solomon asks for an understanding heart.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Tyre
places.summary: Hiram is king of Tyre. He sends Solomon cedar and cypress wood in chapter 5. Solomon brings Hiram the bronze worker from Tyre in chapter 7.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Gezer
places.summary: Pharaoh takes Gezer, burns it, and gives it to his daughter in chapter 9. She is Solomon’s wife. Solomon then builds Gezer with forced labor.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Edom · broad region
places.summary: Joab kills the males of Edom in David’s time. The child Hadad, of Edom’s royal family, flees to Egypt. In chapter 11 the LORD raises Hadad against Solomon.
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Hiel the Bethelite builds Jericho in chapter 16. He loses his firstborn and his youngest son. The chapter says this matches the LORD’s word by Joshua.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: En Rogel · proposed spring locality
places.summary: Adonijah kills sheep and cattle by a stone beside En Rogel in chapter 1. He invites his brothers to the feast but not Solomon.
places.limits: The marker shows a proposed site for the spring.

places.name: Gilead · broad region
places.summary: Gilead lies east of the Jordan. Elijah the Tishbite is one of its settlers in chapter 17.
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.

places.name: Dan · broad northern locality
places.summary: Jeroboam puts one gold calf in Dan in chapter 12. The people go as far as Dan to worship before it.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location in the north.

places.name: Sidon
places.summary: Jezebel is the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. Ahab marries her in chapter 16 and serves Baal.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Gihon · Jerusalem spring
places.summary: Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon king at Gihon in chapter 1. The people blow the trumpet and shout, “Long live King Solomon!”
places.limits: The marker shows the general location of this spring at Jerusalem.

places.name: Anathoth · proposed locality
places.summary: Solomon sends Abiathar the priest to his fields at Anathoth in chapter 2. Abiathar had helped Adonijah. Solomon spares his life but ends his work as priest.
places.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.

places.name: Lebanon · broad mountain region
places.summary: Solomon asks Hiram for cedar trees from Lebanon in chapter 5. Solomon sends thirty thousand men there in turns to work.
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide mountain region, not one spot.

places.name: Succoth · proposed locality
places.summary: The bronze pieces for the temple are cast in clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan. Chapter 7 puts this ground in the plain of the Jordan.
places.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.

places.name: Zarethan · locality uncertain
places.summary: The bronze pieces for the temple are cast in clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan. Chapter 7 puts this ground in the plain of the Jordan.
places.limits: The town’s location is not certain. The marker shows a general area.

places.name: Galilee · broad region
places.summary: Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee in chapter 9. Hiram comes from Tyre to see them, and they do not please him.
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.

places.name: Hazor
places.summary: Solomon uses forced labor to build Hazor in chapter 9. The same list names Megiddo and Gezer.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Megiddo
places.summary: Solomon uses forced labor to build Megiddo in chapter 9. The same list names Hazor and Gezer.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Ezion Geber · disputed Gulf of Aqaba locality
places.summary: Solomon builds ships at Ezion Geber in chapter 9. It is beside Eloth on the Red Sea, in the land of Edom. Jehoshaphat’s ships wreck there in chapter 22.
places.limits: Its site on the Gulf of Aqaba is disputed. The marker shows a general area.

places.name: Egypt · broad region
places.summary: Hadad and Jeroboam each flee to Egypt in chapter 11. Shishak king of Egypt attacks Jerusalem in chapter 14.
places.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.

places.name: Damascus
places.summary: Rezon and his men settle in Damascus and rule there in chapter 11. In chapter 15 Ben Hadad lives there. Asa sends him silver and gold.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Shiloh
places.summary: Ahijah the prophet is called the Shilonite in chapter 11. Jeroboam’s wife goes to his house in Shiloh in chapter 14.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Zeredah · locality uncertain
places.summary: Jeroboam the son of Nebat is an Ephraimite of Zeredah. Chapter 11 names the town once.
places.limits: The town’s location is not certain. The marker shows a general area.

places.name: Shechem
places.summary: All Israel comes to Shechem to make Rehoboam king in chapter 12. The people ask for lighter work, and he refuses. Jeroboam later builds Shechem and lives there.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Bethel · proposed locality
places.summary: Jeroboam sets a gold calf and an altar in Bethel in chapter 12. A man of God from Judah speaks against the altar in chapter 13. An old prophet who lives in Bethel buries him.
places.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.

places.name: Penuel · proposed locality
places.summary: Jeroboam goes out from Shechem and builds Penuel in chapter 12.
places.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.

places.name: Tirzah · proposed locality
places.summary: Jeroboam’s wife comes home to Tirzah in chapter 14, and her child dies. Baasha, Elah, and Zimri rule from Tirzah. Omri attacks it in chapter 16, and Zimri burns the king’s house.
places.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.

places.name: Ramah · Benjamin locality
places.summary: Baasha builds Ramah to block the way to Asa in chapter 15. He stops when Ben Hadad attacks Israel. Asa’s people carry away its stones and timber.
places.limits: The marker shows the general location of Ramah in Benjamin.

places.name: Geba · proposed locality
places.summary: Asa builds Geba of Benjamin with stones and timber from Ramah in chapter 15.
places.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.

places.name: Mizpah · Benjamin identification uncertain
places.summary: Asa builds Mizpah with stones and timber from Ramah in chapter 15.
places.limits: The marker shows a site in Benjamin. That choice is not certain.

places.name: Gibbethon · locality uncertain
places.summary: Gibbethon belongs to the Philistines. Baasha kills Nadab during an attack on it in chapter 15. In chapter 16 the army camped there makes Omri king.
places.limits: The town’s location is not certain. The marker shows a general area.

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: Omri buys a hill from Shemer and builds Samaria in chapter 16. Ahab rules there and builds a house for Baal. Ben Hadad attacks the city in chapter 20. Ahab is buried there in chapter 22.
places.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.

places.name: Cherith · broad eastern Jordan setting, exact brook unknown
places.summary: Elijah hides by the brook Cherith in chapter 17. Ravens bring him bread and meat. He leaves when the brook dries up.
places.limits: The exact brook is not known. The marker shows a wide area east of the Jordan.

places.name: Zarephath · coastal locality
places.summary: The LORD sends Elijah to a widow in Zarephath in chapter 17. Her meal and oil do not run out. Her son stops breathing, and Elijah prays until he lives again.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location on the coast.

places.name: Mount Carmel · broad mountain setting
places.summary: Elijah meets the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel in chapter 18. The LORD’s fire burns up Elijah’s offering. Elijah then prays on the top, and rain comes.
places.limits: The marker stands for the whole mountain. The exact spot is not known.

places.name: Kishon · broad river setting
places.summary: Elijah brings the prophets of Baal down to the brook Kishon in chapter 18. He kills them there.
places.limits: The marker stands for the river as a whole. The exact spot is not known.

places.name: Jezreel
places.summary: Ahab rides to Jezreel in the rain in chapter 18, and Elijah runs ahead. Naboth’s vineyard lies next to Ahab’s palace there in chapter 21. Ahab takes it after Naboth is stoned.
places.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.

places.name: Horeb · traditional Sinai region, identification disputed
places.summary: Elijah travels forty days and nights to Horeb, God’s Mountain, in chapter 19. He stays in a cave. The LORD speaks to him there and gives him new work.
places.limits: The marker follows the traditional Sinai region. The mountain’s location is disputed.

places.name: Abel Meholah · proposed locality
places.summary: Elisha the son of Shaphat is from Abel Meholah. Elijah finds him plowing in chapter 19 and puts his mantle on him.
places.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.

places.name: Aphek · battle locality uncertain
places.summary: Ben Hadad brings the Syrians to Aphek to fight Israel in chapter 20. Israel wins. The Syrians flee into the city, and its wall falls on them.
places.limits: The location of this battle town is not certain. The marker shows a general area.

places.name: Ramoth Gilead · locality disputed
places.summary: Ahab and Jehoshaphat go to fight Syria for Ramoth Gilead in chapter 22. An arrow strikes Ahab in the battle, and he dies at evening.
places.limits: The town’s location is disputed. The marker shows a general area.

contextGuide.description: Explore the book’s larger concerns through selected passages and relevant evidence.

steps.title: A temple depends on skilled workers
steps.text: Verse 14 introduces the craftsman by his parents. His mother was an Israelite widow, and his father a man of Tyre. The verse says he was filled with wisdom, understanding, and skill. Exodus 31:3 uses the same three terms for Bezalel, who built the tabernacle. So the text counts a metalworker’s skill as a kind of wisdom. A man of two peoples makes the temple’s bronze. The bronze stand shown is a regional comparison, not a temple vessel.

steps.title: The divided kingdom begins with a labor complaint
steps.text: The people’s request in verse 4 is an offer, not a revolt. They will serve the new king if he eases the labor. The elders see that the king must first serve them (verse 7). Rehoboam chooses the harsh answer in verse 14. Verse 15 adds that the turn of events came from the LORD. The text names both the king’s folly and God’s purpose. The cry in verse 16 repeats Sheba’s words from 2 Samuel 20:1.

steps.title: An inherited field is more than a commodity
steps.text: Ahab’s offer in verse 2 is fair as a sale. Naboth’s refusal in verse 3 rests on something else. The field is his fathers’ inheritance, and he calls on the LORD. Leviticus 25:23 and Numbers 36:7 keep such land within the family. Ahab sulks (verse 4), and Jezebel asks whether he rules Israel (verse 7). The tablet shows an ordinary field sale, the kind Naboth refuses. She then uses Israel’s own court forms, with two witnesses, to kill (verses 9–10).
